statement: Whenever sort_people(names, heights) returns a result r, let n = len(names). Then len(r) = n, and there exists a sequence p of length n that is a permutation of {0,1,...,n-1} such that for every k with 0 <= k < n, r[k] = names[p[k]], and for every k with 0 <= k < n-1, heights[p[k]] > heights[p[k+1]].
preconditions: Let n = len(names). The following hold: len(heights) = n; 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= len(names[i]) <= 20, every byte of names[i] is an ASCII code of an English letter (65..90 or 97..122), and 1 <= heights[i] <= 100000; for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < n, heights[i] != heights[j].
